## Natural history notes

A small hidden-snout weevil characterized by a compact dark body, hard wing covers, and a short curved snout that can be tucked downward or partly hidden. In Florida and the broader southeastern United States, Rhynchus apiculatus is part of the weevil fauna and is most likely encountered in warm wooded or shrubby habitats with leaf litter, dead plant material, and low vegetation. Its specific host plants and larval biology appear poorly documented, so it is best treated cautiously as a small plant-associated weevil whose adults likely feed on plant tissue while larvae may develop concealed in plant material, seeds, stems, or soil near host plants.
